chapters.summary: Jesus Christ reveals through John the things that must shortly come to pass; from the isle of Patmos John writes to the seven churches of Asia, proclaiming Christ's coming and his glory.
keyPoints: This is the revelation of Jesus Christ, unveiling the prophecy of the last days and God's plan of redemption.
John receives this vision on the island of Patmos and writes it down for the seven churches.
Christ appears in glorious splendor, holding the keys of death and Hades, and grants grace and peace.
chapters.application: You don't need to fear the future, because the Lord reigns over all things. Make a practice of reading Revelation, hold fast to the certainty of Christ's victory, and let faithfulness and hope mark your everyday life.

chapters.summary: Revelation 2 records Christ's words of exhortation and warning to the churches of Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamos, and Thyatira, calling each of them to remain faithful to the end.
keyPoints: The church at Ephesus has abandoned its first love and is called to repent and do the works it did at first.
The church at Smyrna suffers tribulation and poverty, yet the Lord urges them to remain faithful even to death and receive the crown of life.
The churches at Pergamos and Thyatira are tolerating false teaching and sexual immorality and are called to repent and return to the truth.
chapters.application: Examine your own heart to see whether you have lost your first love. Hold on to your faith under pressure, stay clear of false teaching, and overcome through the Lord's strength.

chapters.summary: This chapter records John's messages to the churches at Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea, calling believers to stay watchful, hold fast, and repent.
keyPoints: The church at Sardis has a reputation for being alive but is actually dead; it is called to remember what it received, hold it fast, and repent.
The church at Philadelphia has little strength but has kept the Lord's word, and is given an open door and the promise of being kept from the hour of trial.
The church at Laodicea is neither cold nor hot, and the Lord counsels them to buy gold refined in the fire, white garments, and eye salve, rebuking and disciplining them in love.
chapters.application: Take stock today of whether your faith is genuinely on fire. Listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches, open your heart to the Lord, welcome his discipline, and live as an overcomer.

chapters.summary: In this vision John sees a door standing open in heaven, and, caught up in the Spirit, beholds God on his throne worshiped by the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders.
keyPoints: John is called up into heaven and sees the throne there, and the glory of the one seated on it.
Twenty-four elders and four living creatures surround the throne, worshiping God day and night.
The living creatures and the elders lay their crowns before the throne, praising God as the Creator of all things.
chapters.application: Whatever your earthly circumstances, the throne in heaven stands forever. Let your daily life honor the Lord of creation through worship and obedience.

chapters.summary: This chapter portrays the vision before the heavenly throne, where only the Lamb who was slain is worthy to open the scroll and break its seven seals, revealing Christ's redemption and power.
keyPoints: The one seated on the throne holds a scroll written on both sides and sealed with seven seals, and no one is found able to open it.
John weeps because no one is worthy to open the scroll, until an elder comforts him: the Lion of the tribe of Judah has prevailed.
The Lamb comes and takes the scroll from the hand of the one on the throne, and the four living creatures and twenty-four elders fall down in worship, singing a new song of praise.
chapters.application: When your circumstances seem to have no way forward, remember that Christ has already triumphed and is worthy to open the book of your life. Rest in worship, and let him hold your tomorrow.

chapters.summary: The Lamb opens the first six seals, unleashing war, famine, death, and cosmic upheaval, signs that the judgment of the last days is drawing near.
keyPoints: The first seal releases a white horse symbolizing conquest, and the second seal a red horse bringing war and conflict.
The third seal releases a black horse bringing famine, and the fourth seal a pale horse ruled by Death and Hades.
The fifth seal reveals martyrs crying out for justice, and the sixth seal brings heaven and earth shaking as people flee in terror from the wrath of the Lamb.
themes: The Judgment of the Last Days
chapters.application: In the face of the world's upheaval and suffering, hold on to your faith, knowing that God reigns, and look forward to the justice and comfort Christ will bring at his return.

chapters.summary: This chapter records God sealing 144,000 from the tribes of Israel, and a vision of a countless multitude from every nation, clothed in white, worshiping before the throne — showing the reach of salvation to the whole world.
keyPoints: Four angels hold back the four winds of the earth, waiting until the servants of God have been sealed, showing God's care for both his own people and the whole earth.
144,000 are sealed from the tribes of Israel, a number signifying the completeness of God's protection over his people.
A countless multitude from every nation and people, robed in white, praises God before the throne, their robes washed clean in the blood of the Lamb.
chapters.application: Whatever your circumstances, God knows those who are his and gives them protection and hope. Look to him in faith, keep yourself pure in the midst of trouble, and wait for the day you will join the whole company of saints in worship.

chapters.summary: The Lamb opens the seventh seal and heaven falls silent for about half an hour; seven angels are given seven trumpets, and their blasts unleash a series of plagues warning the world to repent.
keyPoints: The seventh seal is opened and heaven is silent for half an hour, a solemn hush before judgment.
An angel offers up the prayers of all the saints, and incense and smoke rise before God.
The seven trumpets sound one after another, and their plagues strike the earth, the sea, the rivers, and the sun, moon, and stars.
chapters.application: Even amid suffering and judgment, God still hears prayer. When the world is shaken, pray all the more earnestly and hold on to your faith, for God is in control and his purposes will surely stand.

chapters.summary: Revelation 9 describes the fifth and sixth angels sounding their trumpets, releasing locusts from the bottomless pit and horsemen from the Euphrates, bringing judgment and torment.
keyPoints: The fifth trumpet sounds; a star falls and opens the bottomless pit, releasing locusts that are permitted to harm only those without the seal of God on their foreheads.
The locusts torment people like scorpions for five months, and in their agony people seek death but cannot find it.
The sixth trumpet sounds, releasing four angels who lead an army of two hundred million horsemen; a third of mankind is killed, yet the rest still refuse to repent.
chapters.application: In the face of the world's suffering and judgment, stay watchful and repentant, keep your faith, and don't let pain drive you to despair — God remains in control of it all.

chapters.summary: John sees a mighty angel holding a little scroll; seven thunders speak but John is forbidden to write down what they said. The angel declares there will be no more delay, and John eats the scroll, sweet as honey in his mouth but bitter in his stomach — a sign that he must prophesy again about many peoples, nations, tongues, and kings.
keyPoints: A mighty angel comes down from heaven, wrapped in a cloud with a rainbow over his head, planting one foot on the sea and one on the land, and crying out like a roaring lion.
Seven thunders speak, and John is about to write down what they said, but he is told to seal it up — a hidden mystery not yet to be revealed.
The angel declares that the mystery of God will be finished; John eats the scroll, finding it sweet in his mouth but bitter in his stomach — a picture of the cost of his calling.
chapters.application: Receiving God's word may bring sweetness at first, but living it out can be bitter. Ask the Lord for courage to proclaim his truth faithfully, without backing down even when it's hard.

chapters.summary: John is commanded to measure the temple; two witnesses prophesy, are killed, and are then raised and taken up to heaven; the seventh trumpet sounds, announcing the coming of God's kingdom.
keyPoints: John measures the temple, while the Gentiles trample the holy city underfoot for forty-two months.
Two witnesses prophesy for 1,260 days, and fire comes out of their mouths to consume their enemies.
After the witnesses are killed, they are raised to life and taken up into heaven; a great earthquake follows, and the seventh trumpet sounds.
chapters.application: Whatever your circumstances, God watches over his witnesses. Proclaim the truth faithfully, trusting that God will ultimately triumph and his kingdom will come.

chapters.summary: Through the vision of the woman, the dragon, and the male child, this chapter portrays the birth of Christ, Satan's fall from heaven, and the spiritual battle in which believers overcome.
keyPoints: The woman represents Israel, the dragon represents Satan, and the male child foreshadows Christ.
Michael and his angels fight the dragon, and Satan is cast down, losing his place in heaven.
Believers overcome the accuser by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony.
chapters.application: Whatever challenges you face today, remember that God has already promised victory. Trust in Christ's saving work, hold fast to your testimony with courage, and do not fear the accusations of the enemy.

chapters.summary: This chapter describes two beasts rising from the sea and from the earth, representing the antichrist and the false prophet. They deceive the world and persecute the saints, yet in the end remain subject to God's sovereign rule.
keyPoints: The first beast rises from the sea, with ten horns and seven heads, resembling a leopard, a bear, and a lion; the dragon gives it authority, and it blasphemes God and overcomes the saints.
The second beast rises from the earth, with two horns like a lamb but speaking like the dragon; it performs great signs and causes people to worship the first beast.
The beast's mark and the number 666 control buying and selling, symbolizing economic and spiritual domination of the world — yet believers are called to patience and faith.
chapters.application: When you face the world's pressures and temptations, hold fast to your faith rather than drifting with the crowd. Learn to see through deception, stand firm on the word of God, and remain faithful even in hardship.

chapters.summary: This chapter shows the Lamb standing with the 144,000, angels proclaiming the eternal gospel and announcing the fall of Babylon, and a vision of harvest that foreshadows the final judgment and the triumph of God's people.
keyPoints: The Lamb stands with the 144,000 on Mount Zion; they sing a new song, the firstfruits of redemption.
Three angels proclaim in turn: the eternal gospel, the fall of Babylon, and God's wrath on those who worship the beast.
The Son of Man, seated on a cloud, reaps the harvest, and an angel gathers the grapes — images of the final judgment and the ingathering of the righteous.
chapters.application: In the turmoil of these last days, hold on to your faith and do not follow the world or its idols, for the Lord will surely return to bring justice. Stay watchful and ready, be counted among the firstfruits who belong to him, and look forward to eternal rest.

chapters.summary: John sees the sea of glass in heaven and the seven angels who receive the seven bowls full of God's wrath, the foreshadowing of the final seven plagues.
keyPoints: Beside the sea of glass, those who have overcome the beast sing the song of Moses and of the Lamb, celebrating God's justice and salvation.
Seven angels come out of the temple and receive the seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God, marking the solemn majesty of the final judgment.
The temple is filled with the glory and smoke of God, and no one can enter it until the seven plagues are completed, showing the gravity of this judgment.
chapters.application: When you face suffering and injustice in the world, trust that God's righteous rule still stands. As you wait, prepare your heart with praise and obedience, confident that God will surely accomplish his purpose.

chapters.summary: John watches seven angels pour out seven bowls full of God's wrath, bringing one plague after another, until the great city of Babylon falls, paving the way for Christ's return.
keyPoints: The first angel pours out his bowl and painful sores break out on the wicked; the second turns the sea to blood, and every living thing in it dies.
The third bowl turns the rivers to blood, and an angel declares that God's judgments are righteous; the fourth causes the sun to scorch people, yet they still blaspheme God.
The sixth bowl gathers the kings of the earth to Armageddon; the seventh brings a great earthquake, the fall of Babylon, and a devastating hailstorm.
chapters.application: When you see injustice in the world, trust that God's judgment is righteous. At the same time, stay watchful, keep yourself ready, and live a holy life — for the Lord is coming soon, and he calls us to be overcomers.

chapters.summary: Through the vision of the great harlot of Babylon, this chapter exposes the corruption and coming end of worldly power, and calls the saints to remain faithful.
keyPoints: An angel shows John the great harlot seated on many waters, representing the worldly power that deceives the nations.
Arrayed in purple and scarlet, the harlot is drunk with the blood of the saints, revealing her persecution and corruption.
The beast and the ten kings will come to hate the harlot and lay her waste, so fulfilling the words of God.
chapters.application: See through the empty promises of worldly temptation and refuse to compromise with sin. Stand firm in your faith even under persecution, for God will surely judge all evil and give victory to those who follow the Lamb.

chapters.summary: This chapter announces the downfall of the great city of Babylon: because she corrupted the nations, God judges her and repays her double for what she has done.
keyPoints: An angel announces the fall of the great city Babylon, now become a dwelling place for demons.
God remembers her sins and repays her double according to her deeds.
The saints in heaven rejoice over God's judgment on Babylon, for she had shed the blood of the saints.
chapters.application: Do not covet the world's vanity and sin; hold on to holiness instead, for God will judge every wrong. Give thanks that righteousness prevails, and live each day watchfully.

chapters.summary: This chapter depicts the multitude in heaven praising God for judging Babylon, the announcement of the marriage of the Lamb, and Christ's coming as King of kings to defeat his enemies.
keyPoints: The multitude in heaven cries out in praise because God has judged the great harlot.
The marriage of the Lamb is announced, and believers are graciously given fine linen, bright and pure, to wear.
Christ comes riding a white horse and defeats the beast and the false prophet, while the rest are slain by the sword from his mouth.
themes: The Marriage Supper of the Lamb
chapters.application: In the face of injustice, trust that God will judge. Look forward to the Lord's return, keep yourself holy, and wait for the victorious King with praise and faithfulness.

chapters.summary: This chapter tells of Satan being bound for a thousand years, believers reigning with Christ, and the final vision of judgment before the great white throne.
keyPoints: An angel binds Satan for a thousand years and casts him into the bottomless pit, so that he can no longer deceive the nations.
Blessed are those who share in the first resurrection; they reign with Christ as priests for a thousand years.
After the thousand years, Satan is loosed for a short time before finally being thrown into the lake of fire, while the unbelieving are judged before the great white throne.
chapters.application: As you face these end-time prophecies, hold on to hope and reverence, keep your faith firm, and live out Christ's testimony — knowing that righteous judgment will surely come.

chapters.summary: John sees a new heaven and a new earth, the holy city new Jerusalem coming down from heaven, and God dwelling with his people, wiping away every tear as he makes all things new.
keyPoints: A new heaven and a new earth replace the old, and there is no longer any sea.
The holy city, new Jerusalem, comes down from God out of heaven, prepared and ready.
God himself will dwell with his people and wipe away every tear; there will be no more death, mourning, crying, or pain.
chapters.application: In the midst of suffering, take hold of hope, for God has promised to make all things new and to dwell with us himself, wiping away every tear from our eyes.

chapters.summary: This chapter portrays the river of life and the tree of life in the new Jerusalem, reaffirms Christ's coming return, and urges believers to remain holy, closing with the words, 'Even so, come, Lord Jesus.'
keyPoints: The angel shows John the river of life and the tree of life, whose leaves are for the healing of the nations.
The throne of God and of the Lamb is in the city, and his servants serve him and see his face.
Jesus declares that he is coming quickly, bringing his reward with him, urges people to keep the words of this prophecy, and closes with a blessing.
chapters.application: May we always hold on to hope, living holy lives as we wait for the Lord, being renewed daily in grace, faithfully completing what he has entrusted to us, and joyfully welcoming that day.
